Abort

/uh-BORT/ - rhymes with sport · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Abort means to give up on a half-finished project or effort.

When the crosswind gusted past the safety limit, the pilot chose to abort the landing and climb away for another circuit.

Worked Example

The mission director aborted the balloon launch at two minutes to release, with the envelope half filled, after the telemetry link dropped for the third time.

Abort is sharper than stop or cancel because it means ending an effort that is already underway — the launch had begun and was deliberately cut off mid-course, not merely rescheduled before it started.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

scrap: cancel at any stage — even a plan that never left the drawing board

discontinue: stop making or offering something, often winding down gradually

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

complete: carry an effort through to the finish

resume: take a halted effort back up again

Where it sits · how final the stop is — pause → shelve → abort

pause vs. abort: Pause is the gentlest stop — the work waits a moment and then goes on exactly where it left off.

shelve vs. abort: Shelve is milder than abort: a shelved project sits unfinished but alive, waiting for a better season, while an aborted one is ended for good, mid-course.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — ab-

Prefix — ab-: away, amiss

Root — ort

Root — ort: to rise, to come into being (Latin oriri)

Put it together

Put it together: Ab- (away, amiss) + ort (to rise, come into being, from Latin oriri) = to fail of rising — to keep something that has begun from ever fully arriving. The same root gives origin, the point where a thing first arises, and orient, named for the side of the sky where the sun comes up. An aborted effort is one that rose partway and was put away unfinished.

Use the root in a new word: origin

Use the root in a new word: origin: Historians trace the origin of the alphabet to traders who needed a quick way to keep receipts.

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral / technical

Abort is the crisp word pilots, surgeons and engineers use for stopping something already in motion — an approach, a launch, a rollout. It insists the effort was live and was ended mid-course, on purpose. For casual plans, 'call off' sounds more natural, and scrap covers plans killed before they ever start — which abort, strictly, does not.
